classification.difficultyReason: Combine a compass perpendicular construction with perpendicular diameters to construct an inscribed square.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Construct a large circle with centre $O$.

answer.short: A compass-drawn circle with its centre labelled $O$.
answer.worked: Mark $O$. Set the compasses to a suitable radius and draw a complete circle centred at $O$. Keep the circle for part b.

spec.description: Authored example of the requested circle; the source supplies no figure.
spec.mathematics: A circle with marked centre O and arbitrary radius.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Using a ruler and compasses only, construct a square $ABCD$ with all four vertices $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ on the circle.

answer.short: Construct perpendicular diameters $AC$ and $BD$, then join $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ in order.
answer.worked:
Draw a straight line through $O$, meeting the circle at $A$ and $C$. With centres $A$ and $C$ and the same compass opening greater than $AO$, draw intersecting arcs above and below $AC$. Join the two arc intersections. This perpendicular bisector passes through $O$; label its intersections with the circle $B$ and $D$. Join $AB$, $BC$, $CD$ and $DA$, retaining the construction arcs.

The four triangles around $O$ each have two sides equal to the radius and an included right angle, so they are congruent. Consequently the four chords are equal. Each triangle has base angles $45^\circ$, so each angle of $ABCD$ is $90^\circ$. Thus $ABCD$ is a square.

spec.description: Completed inscribed square with perpendicular diameters and retained equal-radius compass arcs. This is an authored answer figure, not a source visual.
spec.mathematics: AC and BD are perpendicular diameters meeting at O. Equal-radius arcs centred at A and C construct the perpendicular bisector of AC. Consecutive circumference points form square ABCD.
